title: 东北硬菜②铁锅炖：一口锅比脸盆还大，炖下整个冬天 | Northeast Comfort Food P2 · Iron-Pot Stew 🍲
description:
铁锅炖，你站炖鱼派，还是炖排骨派？ / Iron-pot stew: team fish, or team ribs?

第②集·铁锅炖 —— 「东北硬菜」系列，每天一道东北招牌菜。
P2 · Iron-Pot Stew — from the series Northeast Comfort Food: one Dongbei classic a day.

东北人炖菜，一口大铁锅比脸盆还大。最早在白山黑水间渔猎的满族先民，就用篝火架起大铁锅，把猎到的、采到的一锅同煮。定居之后，东北民居发展出「灶炕合一」——外屋的灶台连着里屋的火炕，一锅炖菜的同时，热量顺着烟道把炕烧热，饭做了，屋也暖了。最见功夫的是锅边贴一圈玉米饼子：下半截泡在汤里吸满油香，上半截被水汽蒸熟、被铁锅烤脆，菜饭一锅同熟，这就是「一锅出」。咕嘟咕嘟一大锅，炖下的是东北一整个冬天。
In Dongbei, the stew pot is bigger than your face. The Manchu ancestors who once hunted and fished across the northeast cooked everything they caught or gathered in one big iron pot over an open fire. After they settled, homes developed the “stove-and-kang” design — the kitchen stove connected to the heated sleeping platform, so one pot of stew cooked dinner and warmed the room at once. The signature move: cornbread patties pressed around the pot's rim, bottoms soaking up the broth, tops steamed and toasted against the iron — food and staple done together, what locals call yi-guo-chu, “all out of one pot.” One bubbling cauldron holds a whole northeastern winter.
